question.problem: Consider the straight line with the canonical equation $\frac{x-7}{3}=\frac{y-2}{4}=\frac{z+3}{-7}.$ Find the vector equation of the line.
question.worked_solution:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-7}{3}=\frac{y-2}{4}=\frac{z-(-3)}{-7},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(7,2,-3)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨3,4,-7⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -7\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
